what: The tree's dirty check (git status --porcelain on every record write) can rewrite git's index, leaving it newer than the shard, so the next record's seal check reads the whole index: 7.9 MB on PostHog, and the edit-cost test fails on a fast runner
evidence: PR #131 CI run 39667300495: work-meter.test.ts:233 'an edit pays for the files it names' failed with 'fs readFileSync <top>/.git/index: 0 at 1x, 31060 at 10x'; the new shards.test.ts check shows git status rewriting the index of a file rewritten with its own content, 3 of 3 runs

because: gitState and codeDirty ask git status with --no-optional-locks, so asking never writes the index back
